title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-quality, field-resilient microwave resonators fabricated on germanium quantum well heterostructures, a key component for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Ge quantum wells are a promising platform for hole spin qubits, but integrating high-performance microwave resonators is challenging due to material constraints and magnetic field sensitivity.
method: The authors design and fabricate superconducting microwave resonators on Ge/SiGe heterostructures, characterizing their internal quality factors and resilience to magnetic fields up to several Tesla.
result: The resonators achieve high internal quality factors (>10^5) and maintain performance under in-plane magnetic fields, demonstrating compatibility with spin qubit operation.
conclusion: These resonators are suitable for coupling to Ge hole spin qubits, enabling circuit QED and quantum information processing in this platform.

title: Demonstrating Optical Control Of Complex Phases In A Trapped-ion Qubit
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit, enabling precise phase manipulation for quantum information processing.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but full control over qubit phases is essential for high-fidelity gates and algorithms. Optical control offers a pathway to faster and more coherent operations.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion qubit and apply optical pulses to manipulate the qubit's phase via the AC Stark shift, demonstrating control over both single-qubit and two-qubit phases.
result: They achieve high-fidelity phase control with low error rates, showing that optical phase control can be integrated into trapped-ion quantum processors.
conclusion: Optical control of complex phases is a viable technique for trapped-ion qubits, potentially improving gate performance and enabling new quantum protocols.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Anonymous voting is a key multi-party cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security. This work aims to realize such a protocol experimentally with continuous variables, which are more practical than discrete-variable implementations.
method: The authors implement a two-voter quantum anonymous voting scheme using continuous-variable quantum states (e.g., coherent states) and homodyne detection. The protocol ensures voter anonymity and verifiability through entanglement and quantum correlations.
result: Successful experimental demonstration of anonymous voting with two voters, showing that the protocol achieves the required security and functionality with current continuous-variable technology.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting is feasible with current technology, paving the way for scalable multi-party quantum communication protocols.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: An integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with ITU channel grid for quantum networks.
motivation: Quantum networks require scalable, high-quality sources of entangled photons at telecom wavelengths to enable long-distance quantum communication.
method: The authors demonstrate an integrated photonic chip that generates multiple wavelength channels aligned with the ITU grid, using spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide.
result: The source produces high-purity, indistinguishable photon pairs across multiple ITU channels with high brightness and low noise.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable light source for wavelength-division multiplexed quantum networks, advancing real-world quantum communication.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow or assume simpler noise models.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm that leverages the structure of quantum LDPC codes and achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm demonstrates near-optimal decoding performance with significantly reduced runtime compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum error correction by providing a scalable decoder suitable for near-term quantum devices.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a constant runtime error mitigation technique for quantum computing by restricting the evolution of the quantum system.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require significant overhead. The authors aim to reduce runtime while maintaining effectiveness.
method: They introduce a method that restricts the evolution of the quantum state to a subspace that is less prone to errors, using a combination of dynamical decoupling and symmetry verification.
result: The method achieves constant runtime overhead independent of circuit depth, and demonstrates improved fidelity on noisy simulations and hardware experiments.
conclusion: Restricted evolution offers a practical and efficient error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum computers, though it may not be universally applicable.

title: Distributed Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm On A Quantum-centric Supercomputing Architecture
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) on a quantum-centric supercomputing architecture, focusing on scaling QAOA by distributing computation across multiple quantum processors.
motivation: QAOA is a promising near-term quantum algorithm, but its performance is limited by the size and noise of current quantum hardware. Distributing QAOA across multiple quantum processors could enable solving larger optimization problems.
method: The authors design a distributed QAOA framework that partitions the problem graph into subgraphs, each processed by a separate quantum processor, with classical communication to coordinate updates. They analyze the communication overhead and propose an architecture for quantum-centric supercomputing.
result: Simulations show that distributed QAOA can achieve comparable approximation ratios to monolithic QAOA for certain graph instances, with reduced circuit depth per processor, but with additional classical communication costs.
conclusion: Distributed QAOA is a viable approach for scaling quantum optimization, but practical implementation requires efficient classical coordination and low-latency quantum interconnects.

result: Exact quantum critical states are experimentally realized and observed.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates the feasibility of studying critical states in a controlled quantum simulator.

result: Excitons are formed between Laughlin quasiparticles, demonstrating a new type of composite excitation.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the rich physics of fractional quantum Hall states and their quasiparticle interactions.

title: Towards Practical Quantum Neural Network Diagnostics With Neural Tangent Kernels
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 10 June 2026;

method: The authors apply neural tangent kernel theory to quantum neural networks, deriving analytical expressions for the kernel and studying the training dynamics in the infinite-width limit.
result: They show that the neural tangent kernel can predict training behavior and identify regimes where the network is trainable, offering insights into the design of better quantum machine learning models.
conclusion: The work provides a useful diagnostic tool for quantum neural networks but does not advance core quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Spinon Mediation Of Witness Spin Dynamics In Herbertsmithite

title: Crossover Of Quasi-localized Dynamics And Diffusion In Supercooled Liquids

result: The two dynamical processes are found to be coupled, showing a crossover behavior.
conclusion: The coupling between localized and diffusive dynamics provides new insight into the relaxation mechanisms in supercooled liquids.
